Smooth extension and symmetry coordinates

Exposition, proofs and exercises: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. CC0.

The map identifies two points and has a critical point at zero. Even smooth functions descend through this map, but the attained square variable is initially nonnegative. To obtain functions on the whole coordinate space, we construct an extension operator with one formula valid at every differentiability order. The same operator resolves coordinate parity and the exchange symmetry of two variables. A separate positive construction gives smooth flat majorants for locally bounded data.

The earlier square-descent proof, Lemma 2.1, supplies the integral operator used below. Its argument applies to arbitrary even smooth functions on compact intervals, and we specify the parameter estimates needed here. The complete integral Taylor formula is in When a kernel is smooth. The scalar foundation, Sections 12–13, supplies finite-coordinate calculus, geometric series, smooth cutoffs and uniform convergence of differentiated series. The integration foundation, Sections 15–16, supplies measurability of monotone functions, dominated convergence, substitution and differentiation under an integrable bound.

Write , , for functions whose mixed derivatives of total order at most exist on the interior and extend continuously to the boundary, with the successive normal derivatives given by right differentiation there. The case is allowed. All scalar functions may be complex-valued unless an order inequality is stated.

The geometry of the constructions

Left: with and output , the only possible nonzero reflection terms sample the positive variable at ; all subsequent samples lie beyond the cutoff at . The weights are the signed coefficients of Lemma 1, rather than probabilities. Middle: the square coordinate identifies and ; smoothness at its critical point is supplied by (S14)–(S15). Right: the image of the exchange invariants is . The boundary represents coincident points , and Theorem 6 extends the invariant function smoothly beyond the attained region.
